newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Suharto, minister discuss Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto, minister discuss Busang.

text.p: President Suharto discussed the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province with Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana on Monday, government sources said.
"The discussion touched on Busang," a senior government source, who declined to be identified, told Reuters without elaborating.
State Secretary Murdiono and Cabinet Seretary Saadilah Mursid also attended the 40-minute meeting.

The Mines and Energy Ministry has given Canadian companies Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp until February 17 to settle with their local partners before receiving the go-ahead to develop the find.
Bre-X estimates Busang contains at least 57 million ounces of gold worth over $21 billion at current prices.
Another Canadian mining firm, Placer Dome Inc, has meanwhile proposed a $5.0 billion merger with Bre-X and the head of Placer, John Willson, is currently in Jakarta.
He said on Friday Placer was holding talks with Bre-X on the Busang field.
Asked after his meeting with Suharto on the possibility of the involvement of Placer Dome in Busang, Sudjana said Bre-X and Barrick were still negotiating. He did not mention Placer Dome.
"They are negotiating. We want the nationals of Indonesia to get as much as possible," Sudjana said.
He also said Suharto had ordered him to explain state policy on mining to the public following criticism of its handling of the Busang issue.
"The President ordered me to prepare an explanation on government policy in the mining sector," he said.
"We already have rules governing mining contracts. However, people in general don't know about the contracts," he said.
Some analysts had recently urged the government to let local companies and the government play a key role in the mining sector, which is currently dominated by foreign companies.
Sudjana said his ministry was expected to explain the country's mining policy next month.
"We want to make clear our existing rules," he said, adding that they would be reviewed if necessary.
